later_events.mechanism: amendment: first paragraph restated to read in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard (before: in any capacity in those services; after: in any capacity in or with them)

amendment by striking and inserting words in the first and second paragraphs (Armed Forces, Air Force and Space Force, those individuals, Secretary of Defense design approval, Coast Guard under Homeland Security) and adding a final paragraph on uniform regulations; the substance of the clause is enlarged and continues

clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14 as amended. The paragraphs establish the Air Medal for meritorious achievement in aerial flight, vest design approval and award authority in the Secretaries and designated commanding officers, and limit each person to one medal with bars or devices for later achievements. EO 9242-A (1942-09-11) replaced the first paragraph to cover service in or with the named forces; EO 14085 section 1 (2022-10-03) struck and inserted words in the first and second paragraphs (Army and Navy to Armed Forces, any person to those individuals, Air Force and Space Force added, design approval by the Secretary of Defense, Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when not in the Navy) and added a final paragraph making the regulations of the military departments uniform and subject to Secretary of Defense approval. The substance is therefore enlarged, not ended.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (7 FR 3541, PDF page 1) is Executive Order 9158, Air Medal, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt on May 11, 1942; number, title and date agree with the register row. The order has one inventory clause covering its three paragraphs. Later instruments naming it: EO 9242-A (September 11, 1942), which restated the first paragraph so that service in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard qualifies, and EO 14085 section 1 (October 3, 2022), which further amended the first, second and third paragraphs (Armed Forces, Air Force and Space Force, Secretary of Defense design approval, Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard outside the Navy, and a new final paragraph on uniform regulations). Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order as amended by both instruments with no ending statement. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, so it is claimed in force on 2026-10-14.
